exercise.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Curl
library_steps: Hold one dumbbell at your side, palm forward, free hand on your hip.
Curl the dumbbell to your shoulder, keeping your elbow by your side.
Lower slowly, finish all reps, then switch arms.
exercise.one_line_summary: Standing tall, free hand on the hip; one dumbbell, palm forward, curls from a nearly straight arm to about 124 deg of elbow bend while the upper arm stays by the side.

setup.target: Feet hip-width, knees soft, trunk upright and still.
setup.why: S1 watched trunk and knee movement to stop cheating.
Library step; ACE palms up; the palm-up forearm is where the biceps pulls best (S2 reasoning).

setup.target: Right fist on the right hip, elbow out to the side.
setup.why: Library step; keeps the free arm out of the picture of the working arm.

movement.measure: elev / plane: upper arm hanging, a little forward

movement.tolerance: lean under 5 deg; wrist within 10 deg

muscles.emg: Main flexor measured in the alternating dumbbell curl at 65 % 1RM (S1); activity unchanged across hand positions in unloaded flexion (S2)
muscles.role: Bends the elbow and keeps the palm up; what the exercise is for.

muscles.emg: Active in every curl variant; lower in the dumbbell curl than bar curls (S1)
muscles.surface: Thumb side of the upper forearm.

muscles.role: Holds the upper arm by the side.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Upper arm swings forward at the top.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Front delt takes load; ACE keeps elbows by the sides.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning back to swing the weight
mistakes.why_it_matters: Momentum, not the biceps; S1 policed it.

sources.citation: Marcolin G, et al. 2018. Differences in electromyographic activity of biceps brachii and brachioradialis while performing three variants of curl. PeerJ 6:e5165.
sources.what_it_gave: Standing alternating dumbbell curl vs straight and EZ bar, 65 % 1RM, 3 s reps, elbow range 123 +- 12 deg; trunk and knees policed; EZ > dumbbell for brachioradialis.

sources.citation: Kleiber T, et al. 2015. Front Physiol 6:215, doi 10.3389/fphys.2015.00215 (EMG of biceps brachii and brachioradialis in elbow flexion by hand position).
sources.what_it_gave: 16 subjects, 0-130 deg flexion: biceps the same in all hand positions; brachioradialis share higher only when pronated; supinated = neutral.

sources.citation: American Council on Exercise. Exercise Library: Standing Bicep Curl.
sources.what_it_gave: Palms up, elbows close to the sides, hands to the shoulders, lower slowly.

clip_check.check: Left upper arm still by the side (elev both pictures)
Palm forward / up, no forearm twist
Dumbbell clear of the thigh at the start
Right fist resting on the hip (not floating, not inside)
Biceps is the strongest red in both pictures
